Nos Petrus de Rosemberch prepositus capelle regie omnium sanctorum in castro Pragensi notum facimus vniuersis, ad quos pre sentes deuenerint, quod cum super causis litibus et controuersiis, que inter religiosos frai res abbatem et conuentum monasterii Altiua densis ex vna et dominum Petrum plebanum ecclesie in Horicz super vna domo cum suis pertinenciis ibidem in Horicz sita parte verte- bantur ex alia, in nos tamquam arbitrum arbitratorem et amicabilem compositore m beniuole et roncorditer exlitisset compromissum, tan 151 dem nos matura deliberacione digestoque consilio prehabitis diligen- tique scrutinio seu inquisicione preuia virtute huiusmodi compromissi pronuncciauimus in hune modum, quod memoratus dominus Petrus plebanus prefatam domum in Horicz cum suis pertinences a data presencium ad octo annos continuos, si vixerit, tenere aut possidere debeat pacifice et quiete, de ipsaque mediam libram denariorum in die natiuitatis domini anni.s eisdem vno contextu ac indiuisim iam dictis abbati et conuentui censuare. Quam quidem pronuncciacionem et arhitrium nostrum premissum prefate partes ibidem tune presentes emologauerunt (sic) ipsamque ratam habuerunt et gratam. entries.english:
1371, 31 March, Krumau. — Peter, parish priest of Höritz, submits to the arbitration of Lord Peter von Rosenberg in the dispute pending between him and Hohenfurt Monastery concerning a house and its appurtenant properties at Höritz.

1371, 10 April, Krumau. — Peter von Rosenberg, provost of the royal chapel of All Saints at Prague Castle, settles the dispute pending between Hohenfurt Monastery and Peter, the priest of Höritz, over a house and its appurtenant properties at Höritz.

CXXXIV. Let all who shall have knowledge of this present document know that I, Peter, parish priest of Horicz, regarding all and every cause, suit, and controversy pending on the one side between me and the abbot and convent of the monastery of Altovad, concerning a certain house and its plot there at Horicz, with its fields, meadows, and all appurtenances belonging to that house, on the other side, not concluded or compelled, but of my own good and free will, have willingly submitted from beginning to end to the honorable and noble lord Peter von Rosenberg, provost of the royal chapel of All Saints at Prague Castle, as arbitrator, arbiter, and amicable settler. I promise in good faith, putting aside every pretext for excuse, under a penalty of ten talents, payable to the same lord Peter, to abide by, comply with, and effectively obey his arbitration, pronouncement, and command, and not to act contrary to them for any reason, either personally or through another person. I acknowledge that I shall incur this penalty, now for then and then for now, if I prove contumacious and disobedient in carrying out the aforesaid arbitration. In testimony and confirmation of this matter, and for greater security, at my request I have caused the seals of the honorable lords Hostislav, parish priest at Chrumpnaw, and Bohdanczon, parish priest at Welessin, together with my own seal, to be attached to this document. Given at Chrumpnaw in the year of the Lord 1371, on the Monday after Palm Sunday.

Three small seals hang from parchment strips, all in white wax and damaged: (a) St Catherine; “... Petri ... plebi de Horitt”; (b) St Wenceslas; “... Boh... de Wele...”; (c) St Vitus; “... stislay. [Plbni?] ...”

CXXXV. 1371, 10 April, Krumau. — We, Peter von Rosenberg, provost of the royal chapel of All Saints at Prague Castle, make known to all to whom this document comes that, since the causes, suits, and controversies pending on one side between the religious brothers, the abbot and convent of the monastery of Altovad, and Lord Peter, parish priest of the church at Horicz, on the other, concerning a house with its appurtenances situated at Horicz, had been willingly and unanimously submitted to us as arbitrator, arbiter, and amicable settler, after mature deliberation, considered counsel, and careful inquiry, we have pronounced as follows: The aforesaid Lord Peter, parish priest, shall hold or possess the aforesaid house at Horicz with its appurtenances peacefully and without disturbance for eight consecutive years from the date of this document, if he lives, and shall pay the aforesaid abbot and convent one half-pound of denarii for it, in one payment and without division, on the feast of the Nativity of the Lord each year. When the said period of eight years has elapsed, or if Lord Peter departs this life during those years, then the house in question, with all its appurtenances over which the dispute arose, shall return in every respect to the aforesaid abbot and convent of Altovad and to their possession, notwithstanding any objection, and thereafter they may lease it to any persons according to their will. The parties then present approved this pronouncement and our aforesaid arbitration and held it ratified and pleasing. In testimony and confirmation of this matter, we have caused our seal, together with the seal of the aforesaid Lord Peter the priest and, as witness, the seal of Lord Hostancon, to be attached to this document. Given at Chrumpnaw in the year of the Lord 1371, on the Thursday within the octave of Easter.

Three small seals hang from parchment strips, one in red wax and two in white. The small seal of Peter von Rosenberg is as in CXXXIV; the seals of the priests of Hörlitz and Krumau are as on the preceding document and likewise damaged: “... Petri ... de Hori...” and “S. Hostislay ...”. [The rest is illegible.]
